title: Assessing the Slow Magnetic Relaxation Behavior of LnIII4MnIII6 Metallacrowns

synthesis.procedure: Complex 1 was obtained by slow evaporation of the methanol filtrate remaining after isolation of the parent HoIII6MnIII4MnIV2 cluster. After 3 weeks, brown-black needle crystals were collected and washed with cold methanol. During crystallization, some salicylhydroxamic acid hydrolyzed to salicylate. The reported yield is 10% based on the Ho(NO3)3·5H2O used to prepare the parent cluster. No numerical reagent amounts are given in the main text; a synthetic scheme is only cited as being in the Supporting Information, and the supplied SI file does not contain this procedure.

reagents.name: holmium(III) nitrate pentahydrate
reagents.role: lanthanide source for the parent cluster

synthesis.vessel_or_method: slow evaporation of a methanol filtrate
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Brown-black X-ray-quality needles formed over 3 weeks and were washed with cold methanol. Partial hydrolysis of salicylhydroxamic acid supplied the coordinated salicylate.
synthesis.yield: 10% based on Ho(NO3)3·5H2O used for the parent cluster

properties.summary: Dc data indicate dominant antiferromagnetic interactions at low temperature. Solid-state ac susceptibility is frequency dependent below 5 K, but frozen DMF solution shows no out-of-phase signal above 1.8 K, so the solid-state slow relaxation is attributed to glassy behavior or the onset of magnetic ordering rather than single-molecule magnet behavior. Magnetization at 5 K does not saturate by 5.5 T.

measurements.conditions: extrapolated before divergence of chi' and chi''; zero dc field, 3.5 G ac, 10-1000 Hz

measurements.name: blocking temperature
measurements.conditions: not observed; expected well below 1.8 K from the weak solid-state out-of-phase signal; no out-of-phase signal above 1.8 K in frozen DMF

properties.summary: Dc susceptibility shows low-temperature antiferromagnetic behavior. In frozen DMF, frequency-dependent ac susceptibility and a blocking temperature above 2 K at 1000 Hz are consistent with possible single-molecule magnet behavior. The effective barrier and attempt time give a relaxation time of 26 s at 1 K. Solid-state intermolecular interactions reduce the low-frequency out-of-phase signal relative to the frozen solution.
